title: add benchmark-lab edge-case performance suites and reporting pipeline
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Add new edge-case performance test suites (memory-bound, very short/very long seqs, tiny-batch cold starts) and reporting pipeline integration. No user-facing breaking changes.
description: Motivation: benchmark lab has strong coverage for representative workloads but we've observed gaps for edge-case behavior (very short and very long sequences, extreme memory-bound prompts, tiny-batch cold-starts) that cause occasional regressions in kernel selection and autoscaler decisions. This PR adds curated performance test suites that target those edge cases and a reporting pipeline to ingest results into the benchmark metrics dashboard. Changes include new workload runners, profiling baselines, CI orchestration to run edge suites nightly, and a lightweight reporting ETL that pushes aggregated metrics to the metrics store. Checklist: [x] add edge-case workload definitions and runners, [x] add profiling baselines and golden traces, [x] add nightly CI job and gating, [x] add reporting pipeline job and dashboard wiring, [x] update docs with guidance on interpreting edge-case regressions. Summary of changes: - benchmark-lab/workloads/edge_cases/ (new) contains workloads: tiny_batch_coldstart, long_seq_memory_pressure, short_seq_latency_sensitive, repeat-token-degenerate - benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/edge_cases/ (new) stores golden traces and KV cache baselines for target GPUs - benchmark-lab/ci/edge-suites.yml (modified) adds nightly matrix and gating rules - benchmark-lab/reporting/edge_etl/ (new) ETL job that aggregates per-suite percentiles and failure counts and emits telemetry to internal-metrics. Why this approach: having targeted edge-case suites helps surface regressions that are masked by representative workloads and enables us to tune kernel-selection heuristics and autoscaler throttling logic with concrete signals. How to review: run the new runners locally with `pytest tests/edge_cases` or spin up the nightly CI matrix (jobs/edge-suites.yml) to reproduce failing cases; the ETL has a dry-run mode `--dry` that outputs aggregated JSON to stdout. Performance summary from CI runs on target hardware (p4d and a100 variants): tiny_batch_coldstart median latency 45ms (baseline 47ms), long_seq_memory_pressure 95th p99 memory pressure spike reduced by ~12% after runtime changes, short_seq_latency_sensitive median latency unchanged, repeat-token-degenerate exposes a kernel fallback in 1/120 runs (tracked ENG-1530). Migration notes: this wires results into the benchmark dashboard under `bench/edge-cases` and adds alerting on regressions >5% for medians or p99. Related: ENG-1462 (edge-case test spec), ENG-1530 (kernel fallback investigation).
